acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Insectoids family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Royal Guard, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Wing-Lattice Champion (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Ornate deeply ridged crimson-and-gold shell, translucent functional wings, upright guard posture, and ceremonial spear.

Signature mechanic: Royal Lattice: the Guard connects three resin nodes by flying between them, then dives its spear along only the tautest edge; breaking any node slackens that edge and forces a landing.
battlefieldDuty: Patrol a three-dimensional lattice, using its first functional wings and ceremonial spear to defend one hive route from above.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 retain no wings with shell valves between existing segments; T3 retains closed wing cases as paired reservoirs; T4 retains functional wings with capillary membrane veins; T5 remains wingless with hydraulic abdomen chambers and wax-comb cisterns.

Actions show coherent filling through translucent resin, wet chitin reflection, pressure transfer along existing limbs, controlled jets at caste tools, and visible drainage from the active segment valve.
counterplay: Destroy the announced node or leave the taut edge, then strike the wing root when the Guard lands to reset the lattice. Affinity signal: T1–T4 route a clear fill line from a swelling resin chamber to the active limb; puncture that chamber or open its segment valve after discharge. T5 Queen routes the fill through an abdomen valve into the selected comb cistern; rupture that valve while attendants turn the wingless abdomen, without relying on the Queen's tiny useless limbs.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only blue or glossy chitin without hydraulic construction
Glow-only water treatment without coherent filling, flow, and drainage
Invented wings on T1–T2 or T5 and prematurely open T3 wing cases
Liquid bodies that erase chitin segments, mandibles, or caste limbs
identityInvariants: Segmented chitinous body, mandibled head, compound eyes, four to six limbs, narrow waist, and rear abdomen remain legible across all forms.
Chitin brown and black mature into glossy crimson, iridescent green-black, and amber accents without replacing caste-specific limb shapes.
Chitin, resin, wax comb, translucent wing membrane where anatomically present, and amber remain distinct family materials.
Shell ridging, fluting, resin plating, spiracle vents, and comb-throne structures communicate specialization rather than generic size.
Wing state is tier-specific: T1–T2 have no wings, T3 has closed wing cases, T4 has functional wings, and the immense T5 Queen is wingless.
telegraph: Crimson-and-gold shell ridges align, translucent functional wings pull one lattice edge taut, and the ceremonial spear turns along it.
